summary: To ship GitHub OAuth for your app, you must register a new OAuth app in your GitHub developer settings, configure your callback URL, and implement the standard OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow or device flow. The basic setup is completely self-serve with no provider approval required unless you choose to publish your app on GitHub Marketplace.
difficulty_reason: Registering a basic GitHub OAuth app is entirely self-serve, instantly available from your GitHub profile settings, and requires no provider approval or review.

requirements.text: A personal GitHub account or an organization account with administrative access to register the OAuth app.

evidence.quote: You can create and register an OAuth app under your personal account or under any organization you have administrative access to.

requirements.text: A verified email address on GitHub before authorizing an OAuth app.

evidence.quote: You must verify your email address before you can authorize an OAuth app.

steps.text: In the upper-right corner of any page on GitHub, click your profile picture, then click Settings. In the left sidebar, click Developer settings.

evidence.quote:
In the upper-right corner of any page on GitHub, click your profile picture, then click
Settings
.
In the left sidebar, click

.

steps.title: Access Developer Settings

steps.text: In the left sidebar of the Developer settings page, click OAuth apps.

evidence.quote:
In the left sidebar, click
OAuth apps
.

steps.title: Navigate to OAuth Apps

steps.text: Click New OAuth App (or Register a new application if you haven't created one before).

evidence.quote:
Click
New OAuth App
.
Note
If you haven't created an app before, this button will say,
Register a new application
.

steps.title: Register a New OAuth App

steps.text: Enter your Application name, the full URL to your app's website in Homepage URL, an optional Application description, and your callback URL in Authorization callback URL.

evidence.quote:
In "Application name", type the name of your app.
In "Homepage URL", type the full URL to your app's website.
Optionally, in "Application description", type a description of your app that users will see.
In "Authorization callback URL", type the callback URL of your app.

steps.title: Configure App Details and Callback URL

steps.text: Click Register application to create your OAuth app and obtain your client ID and client secret.
steps.title: Complete Registration

steps.text: Redirect users to https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize with your client_id, redirect_uri, scope, and optional state/PKCE parameters. Exchange the returned temporary code via a POST request to https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token using your client_id and client_secret.
steps.title: Implement the OAuth Authorization Flow

steps.text: Upload a custom PNG, JPG, or GIF logo under 1 MB and set a background color in your OAuth app settings.

evidence.quote: After you create an OAuth app, you can customize the app's badge by uploading a logo and selecting a background color.

steps.title: Customize OAuth App Badge (Optional)

nuances.text: A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps.

evidence.quote: A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps.

nuances.text: Temporary authorization codes expire after 10 minutes.

evidence.quote: The temporary code will expire after 10 minutes.

nuances.text: Access tokens expire after eight hours and refresh tokens expire after six months without use when expiring tokens are enabled.

evidence.quote: The access token expires after eight hours, and the refresh token expires after six months without use.

nuances.text: There is a limit of ten tokens issued per user/application/scope combination, and a rate limit of ten tokens created per hour.

evidence.quote: There is a limit of ten tokens issued per user/application/scope combination, and a rate limit of ten tokens created per hour.

blockers.why_it_happens: If the OAuth app is suspended due to reported abuse, spam, or a misuse of the API, GitHub redirects to the callback URL with an application_suspended error.
blockers.workaround: Contact GitHub support through the GitHub Support portal to resolve the suspension.

evidence.quote: If the OAuth app you set up has been suspended (due to reported abuse, spam, or a mis-use of the API), GitHub will redirect to the registered callback URL using the following parameters...

blockers.why_it_happens: The redirect_uri provided in the authorization request does not match what was registered with the application.
blockers.workaround: Provide a redirect_uri that matches what you registered or leave out the parameter to use the default registered callback URL.

evidence.quote: If you provide a redirect_uri that doesn't match what you've registered with your application, GitHub will redirect to the registered callback URL with the following parameters...

agent_can_do: Implement the OAuth authorization code flow endpoints in application code
Exchange authorization codes for access tokens via API calls
Make authenticated requests to the GitHub API using access tokens
developer_must_do: Log into GitHub and navigate to Developer Settings to create the OAuth App
Configure application names, homepage URLs, and callback URLs in the console
Securely store client IDs and client secrets
